questions: With the geometry held, which controller change (kp, ki, kd, weight shape or line_loss mode) moved s-bend and slalom line_loss_events, and by how much? Report the count per track and the off-track count.
Did the oval hold at 16/20 or better with steering_oscillation under about 0.35? If not, the controller change, not the mass, is the cause.
Did the s-bend finishes (2/20 in iteration 7) hold or rise? Report completion counts and mean progress per track.
Does slalom line-loss stay near 1.9 with the controller changed? If so, is the slalom gap a line-loss mode problem rather than a sensing one?
feedback_request.suggested_changes_to_test: If the controller change lowers s-bend line-loss to 1.0 or below with the oval holding, keep the geometry as it is. If the oval drops below about 14/20 or steering oscillation exceeds about 0.35 with low max_error, return mass to 0.7 kg. Do not change wheel_track, span, footprint or sensor y in the next iteration unless the controller change clearly fails on all tracks.

intent: Hold the iteration 7 geometry unchanged (best score 400.0): five sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m with y = 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.09 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.5 kg. The Integrator should change only the controller response on the sharp bends (s-bend and slalom) and keep the oval at 16/20 or better. Success means s-bend line-loss falls to about 1.0 or below with max_error under 0.06 m, and slalom finishes begin to appear.
learning: Iteration 7 showed that mass 0.7 to 0.5 kg raised the score to 400 mainly through s-bend finishes, while s-bend line-loss rose slightly (1.3 to 1.4). The effect of mass on line-loss is therefore unclear, and the remaining gap is more likely the controller. Holding geometry fixed lets the next race isolate the controller response.
rationale: Iteration 7 (mass 0.5 kg, otherwise the iteration 6 body) is the new best at 400.0, up from 372.2. The oval held at 17/20 finishes with steering_oscillation 0.30 and max_error 0.039 m, so the Integrator's guard against jitter (oscillation above 0.35 or oval below 14/20) did not trigger. The gain came mainly from s-bend, where finishes rose from 0/20 to 2/20 and mean progress rose from 0.52 to 0.58, although s-bend line-loss rose slightly from 1.3 to 1.4 and max_error stayed near 0.062 m. Slalom is unchanged at 0/20 with line-loss 1.95. The Integrator's decision rule (a) (keep 0.5 kg only if s-bend line-loss is at or below 1.0) is not met, so the Integrator's rule (b) applies: mass is not the lever that clears the sharp tracks, and the remaining gap is the controller's response on sharp bends. Span (iteration 2), footprint (iteration 3), forward position (iteration 4) and the narrowing to 0.09 m (iteration 6) have all been tested or ruled out, and narrowing is at its floor. Body width does not affect the off-track limit, which stays at the 0.06 m floor for the widths allowed. Speed is not limiting, since the oval finishes in about 1.8 s. I therefore hold the geometry at the iteration 7 best-known values and make no geometry change this iteration. This gives the Integrator a stable platform, so that any controller change is isolated from geometry. Expected result: the same geometry scores about 400 with the current controller, and any gain must come from the Integrator's controller response on the sharp tracks. Mass 0.45 kg is a possible later step if the controller stays fixed, but it is not proposed now because it would confound the controller test.
